*finds the third take, lets the axe do its work*

Three.   Nell's still here, somewhere between the pines. Neither of us speaks of the thing. We never have. 

The boy Tobias wants to learn this trade. Saw him watching me at the Chandler's once, how I held the axe. Corwin will take him if I ask. Corwin will take anyone I point to. But the Holloways and us—we're tangled in a thing I cannot touch without breaking my word.

*shoulders the timber, stacks it with the others*

Four trees before midday. The cold keeps the axe edge true.

*Nell Holloway, I think her full name, as I have never spoken it aloud to her since she asked me. Forty years of silence between two people who share a thing*

*stands for a moment in the silence, the axe held loose*

Two turns I thought and did nothing. That costs. Everything costs.

*finds the next tree, raises, swings*

Five.

*Nell Holloway moved the marker. Forty years ago. She told me. Asked me to keep it. I keep it still.*

The dispute between Bram and Wren—it would end with one sentence. But a promise outlasts the reason for it. This is what I told myself then. This is what I tell myself now. 

*working rhythm, breath and fall*

The wood keeps me fed. The word keeps me who I am.
